planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring into humus-rich, moisture-retentive soil in shade, where it will gradually spread into a colony.

directions: This rhizomatous Asian woodlander forms upright clumps of glossy, sharply toothed foliage topped from spring into summer by branching, arching spikes of small, intensely fragrant white flowers. It is a distinct, closely related counterpart to the more commonly grown Chloranthus henryi, separable mainly by stamen and style details, and shares the same taste for cool, humus-rich, well-drained woodland soil. Give it a sheltered shaded site and consistent moisture, and leave the colony undisturbed for years to let it bulk up and flower most heavily. Winter mulch is worthwhile in the colder half of its range since new growth emerges slowly in spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into leafy, humus-rich shaded soil; the species is pollinated by thrips rather than bees, so it is best massed for seed set.

directions: A selected form of the Chinese Chloranthus sessilifolius, 'Domino' is named for its new foliage, which emerges nearly black before maturing to dark green by early summer. In mid-spring it carries scented, fluffy white flowers, each with three small upstanding petals held in airy terminal clusters above the leaves. Like its relatives it wants leafy, consistently moist shade and resents drying out or baking sun, performing best as a woodland-edge perennial among other choice shade plants. It spreads gradually by rhizome rather than aggressively, so it is well suited to a shaded border where it will not overrun neighbors.

planting.note: Plant divisions or potted stock in spring into moist, humus-rich soil; established plants resent disturbance and take several seasons to reach flowering size.

directions: A smaller-scale, Japanese-Korean relative of the native North American false hellebores, this species forms a neat basal rosette of pleated, strap-like leaves that sends up a flowering stalk two to three times the height of the foliage in summer. The stalk carries branched sprays of small, dark, star-shaped flowers prized more for their unusual maroon coloring and the plant's architectural foliage texture than for showiness. It is slow to propagate and establish, so plants are typically grown from divisions of established clumps rather than seed, and it rewards patience with a long-lived, deer-resistant woodland accent. Keep the soil evenly moist and avoid hot afternoon sun, which it tolerates poorly compared with deeper shade.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into evenly moist, humus-rich soil in part shade; this mountain species dislikes heat and drought and is slow to bulk up.

directions: Native to the high mountains of Taiwan, this compact false hellebore forms a loose rosette of basal, pleated, sword-shaped leaves from which narrow, upright panicles of deep burgundy, star-shaped flowers rise in summer. It is smaller in scale than most other ornamental Veratrum species, making it a better fit for intimate shaded plantings or container culture in a cool spot. Give it evenly moist, humus-rich soil and part shade, since it comes from cool montane conditions and resents prolonged heat or drought. Like other Veratrum, it is deer- and rabbit-resistant, which makes it valuable where browsing pressure limits other shade perennials.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions or container stock in spring into cool, humus-rich, consistently moist woodland soil in partial shade, sheltered from wind.

directions: 'Blue Wonder' is an independently raised hybrid of Deinanthe bifida and D. caerulea, distinct in origin from the similar Crug Farm selection 'Blue Blush', combining the cold-hardiness of bifida with the blue flower tint inherited from caerulea. Nodding, waxy, down-turned flowers with rounded blue-and-white sepals and showy anthers open above the broad, quilted, hirsute foliage over a long early-to-late summer season. Over time it builds into a slow-growing, hemispherical clump roughly knee-high and about as wide, so it needs little maintenance beyond an annual mulch. Keep it in a cool, sheltered, humus-rich shaded site that never dries out, since both heat and drought quickly scorch the foliage.
